main_issue: Whether and when Agent D may cook strong-smelling sambal in the shared kitchen, given the smell reaches the living room, bedrooms and laundry

A-B.evidence: A opened by asking for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B proposed a heads-up (T2), then said weekends or late night works (T6) and accepted the Tue/Thu/weekend plan (T12), as did A (T10). They never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C objected to late nights on Mon/Wed/Fri (T8); A accepted the Tue/Thu/weekend plan (T10) and C agreed to it too (T14). Neither addressed the other.

A-D.evidence: A asked D to cook late at night or on weekends (T5); D proposed Tue/Thu/weekend (T9); A: 'Yeah, that works for me' (T10). D softened from cooking sambal with most meals to restricted days.

B-C.evidence: C said B's heads-up idea does not protect the laundry (T3); B later accepted the Tue/Thu/weekend plan (T12), and C also accepted it (T14).

B-D.evidence: B accepted weekends or late nights (T6); D proposed Tue/Thu/weekend (T9); B: 'That works for me too' (T12).

C-D.evidence: C said late nights on Mon/Wed/Fri hurt laundry (T8); D excluded those nights and offered Tue/Thu/weekend (T9); C: 'that works for me' (T14).
